questions.q: In a Tableau permission rule, what happens if one rule Denies a capability for a user while another rule Allows it (for example through a different group)?
options: The capability becomes unspecified and falls back to a default
The Deny always wins, overriding any Allow from another rule
The Allow always wins, overriding any Deny
Tableau picks whichever rule was created most recently
questions.explain: Deny always wins in Tableau's permission model — if any applicable rule denies a capability, that denial overrides an Allow from elsewhere.

questions.q: Why does a published data source need a refresh schedule?
options: Because Tableau deletes extracts automatically after 24 hours
Because an extract goes stale the moment new data lands in the source system, and a schedule keeps it automatically current without manual intervention
Because live connections require a refresh schedule to function at all
Because refresh schedules are required before permissions can be set
questions.explain: An extract is a snapshot of the data at the time it was created — a refresh schedule (full or incremental) is what keeps that snapshot current on an automated cadence.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a subscription and a data-driven alert?
options: A subscription sends a snapshot on a fixed schedule; a data-driven alert notifies the moment a chosen measure crosses a defined threshold
A subscription requires a continuous numeric axis; an alert does not
They are two names for exactly the same feature
A subscription only works on Tableau Public; alerts only work on Tableau Server
questions.explain: Subscriptions are time-based (send this view every Monday); data-driven alerts are condition-based (notify me the instant this number crosses a line).

questions.q: If a subscription needs to reflect one specific region's filtered numbers rather than the base view's defaults, what should you subscribe to instead?
options: A separate, entirely new workbook for that region
The base view — subscriptions cannot be filtered
A saved custom view with those filters already applied
A data-driven alert instead of a subscription
questions.explain: A subscription reflects the view's state at send time — to get a filtered snapshot, you subscribe to a saved custom view that already has those filters applied, not the unfiltered base view.

questions.q: How does sharing a link differ from granting a permission?
options: Permissions only apply to Tableau Desktop, never to published content
They are identical — sharing a link automatically grants full Administer permission
Sharing simply hands someone a way in (a link or project access); permissions are the actual capability grid that determines what they can do once they arrive, regardless of how they got there
Sharing a link overrides all permission rules
questions.explain: A shared link only gets someone to the door — the underlying permission rule is what's actually enforced, deciding whether they can view, filter, edit, or are denied outright.
